legend: This complex comprises two anchoring subunits, SDHC and SDHD; the catalytic components SDHA and SDHB; and SDHAF2, which is responsible for flavination of the SDHA component of the complex. If any component of the SDH complex is lost, the complex becomes dysfunctional and SDHB immunohistochemistry becomes negative.

diagnosis: Lymph node metastasis of succinate dehydrogenase–deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST)
legend: Lymph node metastases, uncommon in all other GISTs, are very frequent in succinate dehydrogenase–deficient GISTs and are a clue to the diagnosis.
SDH-deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumours commonly demonstrate a plexiform or multilobulated growth pattern.
Such tumours commonly demonstrate a plexiform or multilobulated growth pattern.
Such tumours are usually epithelioid predominant and demonstrate a lobulated growth pattern.

SDHB immunohistochemistry in a succinate dehydrogenase–deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumour. For a tumour to be considered truly succinate dehydrogenase–deficient, there should be positive staining in the non-neoplastic endothelial cells, which act as internal positive controls.

SDHB immunohistochemistry in an SDH-deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumour. It is emphasized that for a tumour to be considered truly SDH deficient, there should be positive staining in the non-neoplastic endothelial cells, which act as internal positive controls.
